boundary_payload.decision_question: Where should reviewed scientific evidence become durable without mutating the frozen Scientific Foundation V6 baseline?

required_scientific_replay: two frozen Nature primary sources and evidence chain

promotion_protocol: verify exact immutable parent database SHA-256 and schema identity
obtain reviewed source artifacts from external CAS by frozen SHA-256; do not depend on live network refetch for promotion
copy parent snapshot to isolated staging database
replay only reviewed and explicitly authorized entity, assertion, source, claim, review, link and assessment rows
perform all database mutations transactionally on staging only
validate runtime schema identity, quick_check and foreign keys
run full repository regression gates against the staged result
close database and compute final database SHA-256
publish create-only under content-addressed snapshot directory and write canonical sidecar manifest
optionally update active pointer atomically only under a separate activation authorization
never modify or delete the parent snapshot during promotion

recommended_architecture.name: immutable_derived_snapshot_series
recommended_architecture.principle: Every durable scientific promotion creates a new immutable database snapshot descended from a verified parent snapshot.

rejected_default_options.reason: Destroys the frozen reference boundary and invalidates the established V6 byte identity.
Schema version and data-state version are distinct; adding reviewed rows does not constitute Schema V7.
Large mutable/scientific source bytes belong in external data/CAS storage, while Git records policies, manifests and cryptographic identities.
A sparse overlay weakens the existing single-database FK and repository contracts.

snapshot_reproducibility.reason: Authorized persistence metadata such as materialization timestamps may differ between runs; each published snapshot is nevertheless immutable and content-addressed by its own database SHA-256.
